utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question was: When I put the previous document to the witness, the last one to be admitted, which shows that the smuggling of arms in Vlasenica had reached large proportions and the Serb chief of the police station appointed a Muslim police inspector to lead this drive, this gentleman said the document was forged by me and my people who were tearing up Bosnia. My question was: Is it the case that on 24 June, 1991, I was in favour of breaking up Bosnia, and he said yes. And this is a document showing that both Zulfikarpasic and I were fighting for Bosnia to remain together. This was a public debate. It was mentioned with other witnesses. Zulfikarpasic was a long-time democrat. He had emigrated at one point and then returned. We can very briefly summarise this document and see what we both advocated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And your question for the witness, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is, Witness, based on what do you claim that I wanted to see Bosnia divided when you see that on 18 August 1991 I was campaigning to keep Bosnia as it was with a very renowned Muslim politician, leader of a party?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: On what basis do I claim that you were aiming to divide Bosnia? It's not difficult to prove. There were many papers and documents that you passed on to lower levels. By this time you had established everything that a parastate should have in its system. You armed your paramilitaries. You formed your paramilitaries. Now, this is questionable. I don't know if this is an authentic document. Who wrote this? I don't want to testify against this late Adil Zulfikarpasic. I don't want to comment on what you or he said allegedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that we Bosnian Serbs, for the sake of this agreement, gave up all our ideas for regionalisation and all the other measures that had been already announced? Do you know that this was a major campaign that lasted two months, and you knew nothing about it? It lasted the whole of July and August. Zulfikarpasic and I were literally fighting for Bosnia to remain together.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you did fight, and you managed to bring it down. How -- how can you say one thing and do something entirely different on the ground? We know what the facts are, and you are trying to persuade us that you were a peacekeeper, the person who caused the greatest genocide after the Second World War, who misled all the people, all the Serbian people in huge numbers who did not want to follow you originally.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted or MFI'd? This is a news report from that public debate where we said very important things. If I may just quote from the middle of the second column where Zulfikarpasic explains that Izetbegovic had withdrawn his support for that agreement. If I may read it out, or perhaps this can be MFI'd and then it can be useful to you if you want to look into this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, as is the practice of the Chamber not to admit newspaper articles, this is what it appears to me to be. So I would object to it being admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think the practice is not to admit newspaper articles from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In light of the witness's answer that the accused was misleading Zulfikarpasic at the time and Zulfikarpasic was trying to prevent bloodshed in different ways, whether it may be relevant to understand the context of what was happening at the time and given the previous answers of the witness together with the witness's submission -- accused's submission. I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1650, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D4065 is the next document I would like to call up to see that in Vlasenica while you were at the head of the executive authorities there existed, indeed, the Patriotic League. 1D4065. Don't be confused by this date, 9 August 1992, because the document speaks of events that had started much earlier. It says that the Chief of Staff of the PS of Vlasenica, Chief of Staff of the armed forces of Vlasenica, Adil Omerovic, graduated from the maritime academy and came to Vlasenica on 19 May. And then further below -- could we see the next page. You see the first box. The clerk in charge of personnel and personnel affairs, Zaim Aliustic, born in 1963, I suppose, graduated from a teachers' school, reserve officer, completed a course for commanders and has been actively participating since December 1991 in defence preparations of the Patriotic League. And further below all these documents show that the Patriotic League existed in Vlasenica as early as that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This document was written in August 1992. It originated probably in the area of Cerska. I cannot say anything about this document. I was not in Vlasenica then. I was in Tuzla. You can see the date. You can see who drafted it. It has a stamp on it, but I have no knowledge about it. This is the first time I see it. And you also quote names that are not from the municipality of Vlasenica. This man who is a graduate of the maritime academy is not from Vlasenica at all. I know none of these people, and you are trying to put this paper to me as proof that the Patriotic League existed. And by the way, it was not a military organisation. Those were patriots who were trying to convince Serbs and Muslims not to fall for your deception.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see. The staff of the armed forces of Tuzla, armed forces of Vlasenica. Those are the addressees. Is Cerska in Vlasenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there was free territory in Cerska. This man who signed this and put a stamp here lived in Cerska, and there was a section that he authorised to maintain contact with other services.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? It proves that this man was active from December 1991 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not proving anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. The document proves that this man, Zaim Aliustic was active on behalf of the Patriotic League beginning with December 1991. I'm addressing the Chamber now, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you -- Mr. Karadzic, you are using so many untranslated documents. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1651, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your understanding, but this is a witness who is much too baroque as so many things follow from his statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we now see 1D4062, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but I don't understand Mr. Karadzic's last point. This is a document that he listed on his 65 ter list of documents, of cross documents that he's going to use and so they should be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would do it all if we had time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this from the Municipal Staff of the armed forces of Vlasenica, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 19 July 1992? So it's the Muslim segment; correct? At that time, it was no longer a joint municipality.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I don't know where it was from. Cerska, that's where the staff was at the time. It refers to the armed forces of Vlasenica, which should mean the entire complex of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the box in the first paragraph. I quote: "With the order on the disbandment of the original staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the formation of the TO staff of the RBH, Muslim and Serbian staffs were set up based on ethnic criteria. "By 15 April 1992, as a commander -- as commander of the Vlasenica TO, acting on my own orders, I set up our regional defence sector staffs for Djile, Stedra and Vrsinje areas and appointed the commander of TO detachments and anti-sabotage platoons which were set up and mobilised. Their first combat actions against the enemy lasted from the 2nd to the 7th of May, 1992, after which they were smashed and parts of them joined the Srebrenica and Zepa TOs. Meanwhile, from 10 to 21 April, 1992, when the Chetniks stormed the town of Vlasenica, all political business and state leaders fled, leaving the people at the mercy of the occupiers...," and so on and so forth. Do you know this Ferid Hodzic who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I know Ferid Hodzic, but I don't know this document nor can I say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But is it true that this joint TO was disbanded on his orders and two ethnic ones were set up?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Of course not. You know it is not up to local TOs to make such decisions. The republic and regional authorities are the only ones competent and authorised to make such decisions. So this cannot be a true statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that he refers to the disbandment of the regional staff of the TO and the formation of the TO staff -- Muslim and Serbian staff were set up. Do you see that he refers in the first sentence to a republic TO decision?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: If this were proper, he should have invoked a decision published on such and such a date in the republic "Official Gazette" et cetera. He has to refer to the specific decision published in a specific official gazette invoking article such and such of a specific law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have no better opportunity than you for someone from Vlasenica to explain to the Chamber what went on in Vlasenica. You are, perhaps, the only chance for this Trial Chamber to hear a prominent Muslim from Vlasenica who will explain to them what actually happened. Please don't be cross with me. I'm not attacking you. I only want to find out what is what.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1652, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Karadzic, your one and a half hours is up a while ago. How much more do you need to conclude?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I was to complete this properly I would need all day because so much was said on so many occasions that if you are going to give any weight to this witness I need to clarify all this today and to challenge it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Conclude your examination by the end of this session which means by 20 past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I have to skip certain things. Could we now see 1D4064. I will not deal with this document after all. Can we see 1D4065.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this not what we saw before? Yes. That's marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Sorry. Could we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said, Witness, that I used to come and inspect paramilitary units more than once. Do you know that the JNA had at least two major mobilisation drives and that I'm -- and that those units in Milici were from the reserve force of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No. There was one mobilisation drive end of July 1991, although even that was carried out circumventing all proper criteria while the leadership of Yugoslavia should have specified the exact method of mobilisation without calling up Muslims to kill Catholics in Croatia. It is important for the Trial Chamber to know. The first mobilisation was carried out in end June 1991, and then early in July the Vlasenica brigade was sent to Zaluzani near Banja Luka because they were supposed to go to Okucani and further in Slavonia to kill Catholics and the population of Croatia. That is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about Vlasenica, in that region. Please, was the army dividing people there and killing? We'll leave it to the Court to decide. I want to look at one intercept now, although I hate intercepts. It's 65 ter 30461, to show you whether I toured those units or I encouraged state officials to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, unfortunately the interpreters could not hear your previous answer. Could you repeat. When Mr. Karadzic talked about the intercept, you answered in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, before that I'm going to say that the army that was located in Milici was mobilised by the SDS. That is a para-creation. So, Mr. Karadzic, you know full well that you came there every week and stopped at Zvonko's tavern. We knew every moment you were going to Bratunac, Zvornik and all these municipalities. We knew that at every moment. As for intercepts and speeches, Karadzic and Zvonko, if we're talking about December 1991, these are their last conversations. By then everything was done in order to bring all the Serbs together and mobilise them. This has to do with part of the Serb people who were avoiding mobilisation. Zvonko is saying to him that nevertheless, they even made them go and they're inviting him to some kind of party, and he refused that because we know very well what you were doing, you, Karadzic. We know that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How is it that you are aware of this conversation that I haven't displayed yet?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, when I testified for Naser's defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Not only that, Your Honour. It's one of -- this intercept is one of the five intercepts that he listened to before the Krajisnik testimony, which is authenticated in exhibit MFI D1643 now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But did the accused say it was a conversation between him and Mr. Bajagic? Let us see. Let us upload that intercept, 30461.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Witness, how was it that I was covered, as you had it? Was it some state organ that was covering my state organ -- my movements or was it some other organ?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The most ordinary people who were just sitting there and watching what you were doing. These were drunkards who were providing information. This has nothing to do with any state organ. These were drunkards, winos that saw you and your entourage coming and going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, sir, you said that I was covered wherever I went and that you knew wherever I went?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was drunkards, winos, vagabonds that were covering you. They're the people who knew where you were. You liked drinking and carousing too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And these drunkards and vagabonds were providing information to you?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, we know through conversations and people were afraid. I mean every movement of yours instilled fear in people, amazing fear amongst the Muslim people and the Catholic people and whoever. It was fear that you instilled, an incredible fear that I can not explain to the Trial Chamber or to the other persons present here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to take a look at the first page, because the witness seems to be very familiar with this document. Then we're going to move on to the second page. Do you agree you remember in advance although I did not say who my collocutor was, do you agree that during this conversation I am saying that state officials should go and visit JNA reservists, not party officials?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: But of course. You finished everything. You had finished all your preparations and everything and of course you as the top person of the political party was trying to avoid all of that, but you will come. You would come on one day to Zvonko's tavern, and you would stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 365, actually. Can we have that page? That's in Serbian. 2365. That's the ERN number. We haven't got time for all of this. Yes. Now, can we have this long bit where I'm speaking, can we have that in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's on page 3. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking to Koljevic who is in the room, and I'm saying that we helped the army. "The party helped the army to form a volunteer's detachment. There are 600 people and they will hoist the flag at 4.00 tomorrow. The army is there. They're under JNA command. They are wearing JNA uniforms," and so on. Now, it is a volunteer's unit, but we are manning war units. That is going to be a small rally tomorrow and it would be a good thing if one of us went. I think it's better if someone from the state organ go rather than the party and I'm suggesting Ms. Plavsic should go as a member of the joint Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As for this group of 600 or 700 soldiers in Milici, did you say that that was an SDS paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No, no. This was a lot earlier, 1991. That's when units were located in Milici, when they went to the front line in Croatia, volunteers that were mobilised by the SDS. I mean, this is 1991. These people went and then there were people who lost their lives at Vukovar and elsewhere and also became disabled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1653, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is your thesis, Mr. Redzic, that am I right to say that it became that because the Muslims and Croats did not go to do their military service, their compulsory military service, and also they did not respond to the call-up in terms of the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No. The key reason is that it sided with the Serb people and it identified itself with what -- what's his name? With all of Milosevic's ideas. So you could see where the Serb -- or, rather, the JNA was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The Serb population, whatever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I forgot to tell you this, Mr. Redzic, but while you are giving your answers to the questions posed by the accused, you are actually addressing the Chamber. Please bear that in mind, Mr. Redzic. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said today I don't know what the line was, that it had been cleansed of the Croats and Muslims, the JNA. Is that not what you said today?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, practically almost. Very few Catholics and Muslims were left but definitely it had already been cleansed and you know what the reasons were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they cleanse themselves or did somebody else cleanse them?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Milosevic's ideology cleansed them, and also the JNA that served Milosevic's ideology and later on Karadzic in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you take part in this cleansing of the JNA of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No way. No. No. I never had the intention to do that, and also I did not want to allow the Muslim people to go to Croatia to kill Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: D1373. During the first mobilisation in the month of July, did you go to the JNA camp near Banja Luka in an organised way involving two buses, and did you return -- actually, I don't know whether you went personally. Did you send these buses, and did you have these soldiers returned home?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I together with President Stanic. We went with the parents of these children, these soldiers who had been unlawfully mobilised. I -- actually, their objective was to send them against Croatia, Okucani, wherever. The president of the SDS and the president of the municipal assembly were there too. At the time their intentions were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this your signature? Is this the document in which you informed the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that many citizens rallied together and were against mobilisation and there were two buses that were sent there?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, man, two buses? Ten buses went, whatever. But you can see that. What is this signature here? So it is true that I went with ten buses together with Mr. Stanic. Women, children, brothers, sisters, to get the troops that had been deceived and tricked into going to Banja Luka and further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of July, 1991, did you have any authority over the Ministry of Defence of Yugoslavia? Were you allowed to do this kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- actually, I and Mr. Stanic and the chief of the interior, we were informed by the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina that no one should respond to the call-up because negotiations were underway. Once they agree on this, we would be informed. Dispatches were being sent to me and Stanic and the minister of national defence who was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, possibly. This last letter seems a bit suspicious.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you say the number for the next exhibit -- next document? Yes. The interpreters didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4066. The previous document has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that previous document has been marked for identification pending translation, and this seems to be the perfect moment to admit it therefore.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Had you committed a crime when you did what the previous document describes, a crime against the security of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I think that that was not the case, because at that time there was no Yugoslav Army. By then they had definitely sided with the Serb people and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at this. Is this a document of your municipality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the last part of the answer due to your overlap, Mr. Karadzic. What did you say after having said, "By then they had definitely sided with the Serb people, and --"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the SDS in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a document of yours that refers to securing buildings, employees, guards in streets, et cetera? Is this proof, some proof, of an increase in tensions and threats to -- to the security of officials in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I want to have a look at this entire document. I want to see whether it is my own document, and I see here that all the members took part, the Serbs included, but I want to have a look at all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I have the next page, please. If you're done, you ask for the next page.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Could we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1654, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 30339. Could I have that, please. And once again I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to reconsider. You will not have another opportunity of hearing as a witness a high official from Vlasenica. This is the last opportunity of hearing as a witness such an official here, and we will have to deal with Vlasenica considerably, and there is no one who could replace this witness. Sir, take a look at this Tihomir Savkic, probably?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Cavkic, Cavkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. He is talking to Rajko Dukic president of the executive board of the SDS and director of your bauxite company; right?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Cavkic says that there is gunfire there. It's not that exciting, but there is some shooting going on. And Dukic says that we attended a meeting at the Assembly at Krajisnik's office, and that we were all there, myself included. And Dukic says, "What? There is some kind of gunfire?" And Cavkic says, "About 20 minutes ago there was some shooting. About half an hour ago there was shooting." "Where?" "Near our building." "Ah-ha near our building. Was the police notified ...," and so on and so forth. So in the month of October there was shooting, and this man is informing Rajko Dukic about that. Were you aware of that shooting?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I have no idea. This is Sarajevo. This man Cavkic is not from our area, if you think that he's talking about Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You think he's not talking about Vlasenica? Why would he be providing information to Rajko Dukic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Rajko Dukic was president of the SDS, for heaven's sake, man. From all parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina Serbs from Bosnia-Herzegovina are going to be calling him and me. They're not going to be calling me and Alija Izetbegovic and I don't know who else or somebody from the ranks of the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Then we're not going to tender this at all if you don't know where this happened. Can you -- actually, let me put it this way: Did you agree with the Serb Democratic Party and the Serb people to establish two municipalities in Vlasenica, and do you know how many towns exist that consist of two or more municipalities? Do you agree with that, that there are such towns?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, the point is not in having one or two or three municipalities. The point is that a joint entity was being divided into two, a Serb and a Muslim one. I'm sure that all the persons present here have all these documents that show that we were simply doing this for the simple reason, man, that there would not be any kind of excessive behaviour on the part of the Muslim people so you and your followers would use that as a pretext for killings, rape, looting, destruction. That is why this was troublesome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, the Serb side accepted to leave Yugoslavia on the condition that they have their own autonomy in Bosnia. Did you negotiate with the SDS in good faith or were you buying time, and were you deceiving the Serbs as Alija Izetbegovic was telling you, as you had said?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: We're aware of all these stories. What kind of negotiations could be taking place at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Yes or no, did you do it or did you not do it?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no if you put a question to me, I did not have the intention of having Vlasenica divided at all because I knew that nothing would happen if there were to be a division and even if it happened why were 2.400 Bosniaks killed, why were so many women raped, why was there such a great deal of material destruction and looting, whatever. Let us start from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wait a moment. We agreed on the transformation of Vlasenica into a Serbian and Muslim municipality but you didn't mean it seriously?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: -- done under duress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not a place for debate. Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber is not minded to extend the time for your further cross-examination. You have five minutes to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I say with regret that the Trial Chamber deprived me of the right to question this witness properly. This witness has not been questioned. Now, in the remaining five minutes I want to see 3515. And I have to say I don't intend to defend myself in the way my predecessor did. Of course they were convicted. I don't want a make-believe trial. I want a proper trial or none at all. With a witness who is saying this kind of thing, if he's going to be given any attention at all, I want one day to question him on his evidence in Krajisnik and one day on his evidence in my case. With his evidence standing this way, it's no wonder Krajisnik was convicted. The cross-examination in Krajisnik was not good, and he and his lawyer admitted it was not good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... A succession of commentary is just using the time that you could have used to ask a question. You're losing focus.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the document I wanted. I wanted 1D3501. Your Excellencies, with all due respect, it's much more important for me that this trial be fair than to stick to some dead-lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is paying utmost care so that the trial is a fair one. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a document authorising the negotiators to restructure the municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I don't know. The date is on the 13th of April. I believe the document was signed on the 11th of April. This date is 13 April 1992. I don't know who signed it. Could we see the last page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Milenko Stanic signed it. Could we see the next page?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: That's his version and yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You accepted this, but you didn't mean it seriously, did you?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: We meant it seriously. We seriously meant that the negotiations are going no way, that it was pure farce and that you were going to attack us very soon and that the Muslim people would suffer exactly what they suffered later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have it in the papers, but I don't have time for it now. Did Izetbegovic advise you to drag your feet while you evacuate people from Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: We on the ground reported and informed Mr. Izetbegovic, who was not even aware of the situation prevailing in our municipalities. We were telling him what was happening to the Muslim people, and then he said, "Try to buy time as much as possible while you evacuate people towards Kladanj." He wasn't even aware of all this. He believed you more than he believed our people on the ground, and he listened to the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many people did you manage to evacuate before the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know the Vlasenica part of the municipality and the neighbouring villages were evacuated in large part to Kladanj. The area that was closer to Cerska and Nova Kasaba they went to Cerska and Nova Kasaba, but I can't give you the exact figure, how many people managed to leave Vlasenica, but from the reports we got from Cerska, every time somebody would come from there in view of the total number of Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Leave aside Cerska, Kladanj and Kasaba and Konjevic Polje. You managed to evacuate the rest?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: From the town itself people managed to leave, those who intended to, although Serbs had promised to guarantee their safety. Those same people disappeared and no one knows what became of them, 90 per cent of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean those you evacuated?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Best of all, I didn't evacuate anyone. People left on their own after hearing what happened in Zvornik, Bijeljina, Bratunac. People were coming from those areas talking of massacres and killings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted, and see 1D4067.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an inaccurate document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Redzic. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1655, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4067, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for your understanding, Mr. Redzic, admitting a certain document does not mean that the Chamber admits what is contained in the document. We will take into account what you said in the courtroom. And, Mr. Karadzic, I take it this is the last question for you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would like to ask you for two or three very brief questions after this, only with a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your document, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is even my handwriting, but the date is a forgery. This was done before the holiday of Bajram where we gathered and agreed to organise festivities on the occasion of Bajram. And Bajram, if I remember, in 1992 fell on the 4th of April. And here we listed exactly what everyone took upon themselves to do, who would organise the celebration, who would take care of the slaughtering of lambs, and these were festivities that we wanted to invite Serbs to. And Serbs planted a story in some newspaper that Redzic planned the slaughter of the Serbian population, whereas I in my life never even saw a chicken slaughtered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the part where it says this will be Black Friday for the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How come this is suddenly typewritten? This is really ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say call the president of SO Tuzla, Besnagic [phoen] to address our refugees? The General Staff orchestrates all this operation. Columns of refugees, et cetera, to free up Friday --

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: To free children from school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do what next?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Organise a cultural event and festivities on the occasion of Bajram. Look what you encircled, saying that Serbs should be killed. How can you say that? You can see. It's obvious what this writing is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. What is handwriting without the parts that you added in order to label me. This story was even planted in the newspaper, and the newspaper later printed a denial. The newspaper said it was an honourable good man and this whole thing was not at all what it was said to be.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the number Mr. Karadzic called. Speakers are overlapping now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The last question of yours, Mr. Karadzic, and the answer were not interpreted because of the overlap. I would like to repeat -- like you to repeat your question and answer, and I'll -- but before that, could you explain to us what this document is about? It is -- the typewritten part was added by the Defence or by the Serb authority later on?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The Defence got hold of this document the way we see it here. It has been faxed from somewhere, and this is page 2 of a larger document, annex number 12 from some collection. There is a reference to sheep for slaughter, herd for slaughter --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I explain something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Redzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a sheet from an agenda, from a diary. These contents could not be here, especially not in Cyrillic. This was typed in later to create a false picture, for Karadzic to maybe portray me as a terrorist, but fortunately we have very smart, intelligent people sitting here who will not allow that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the handwritten parts are your handwriting. You can confirm that except for the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honours, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Redzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this was a brief presentation where Muslims gathered and everyone was given a specific duty to help organise festivities for the holiday of Bajram. It was not meant against anyone. One person was to procure lambs, and Serbian leaders from the SDS even were invited to these festivities. They ate the meat with us and the sweets too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic, do you remember the part which were not reflected in the transcript, your last question and the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you convicted to ten years' imprisonment by the Military Court for that operation to subvert the defence capabilities of the country and hauling away reservists from the camp in Zaluzani?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: There was a trial and the Military Court, including Major Ostojic, indicted me, and I was defended by lawyer Bajnagic [phoen]. He told me that in my absence I was convicted under the Criminal Code of the SFRY, Article 205, paragraphs 1 and 3, I believe, and that he expects ten years' imprisonment. I never got the judgement in writing, but that's all I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you run away from Vlasenica on the 18th of April because of this and that Milenko Stanic in his own car drove through Serb territory via Tisca away?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I'm not denying about Mr. Stanic. It was agreed, however, that Professor Vukic take me to the territory on the border of Kladanj municipality. However, he did not accept, and he just called me and said, "Good luck, Redzic." And in Tisca, what saved me only God knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then who gave you a lift?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I took Sevko Huric's [phoen] car, Sevko and late cantonal Judge Avdic and another man took the same car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry the Trial Chamber decided to abbreviate this questioning. Maybe you will get a subpoena from us in the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you able to follow -- scroll back the transcript? I'm not sure how important it is, but at page 69, lines 11, 12, there because of the overlap your question and the witness's answer were not reflected in the transcript. If you remember the question, I would allow you to put that question again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the question had to do with the judgement of the Military Court, and I repeated it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have that judgement. We have many other documents. We haven't even touched upon the issue of the conflict in Vlasenica itself. There are many outstanding issues that this witness could help us with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long would you need for your re-direct examination, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any re-examination of the witness, but in relation to the last document, because there was quite a bit of discussion about it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We're going to mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, because there's no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to be satisfied as to its authenticity as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- and provenance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- my next question. I was going to ask Mr. Karadzic. He stated that the Defence got hold of this document but didn't say from where and I would like to know whether he's prepared to tell the Chamber the source of the document, where he obtained the document from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And could we inspect the original?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it's attachment -- or annex number 12 from some collection. I have to research with my Defence the origins of this document. Because it's only going to be MFI'd, we will have time to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll give the number, being marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1656, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, before we break I wanted to correct the record. Transcript page 55, line 14, at least on the transcript that I have in front of me I misspoke when I said MFI D1643. In fact I should have said Exhibit P3190 when I was talking about the authentication sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Redzic, then that concludes your evidence in this trial. On behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. We rise all together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will have a break for 25 minutes and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before the witness is brought in, I just wanted to advise that he should be provided with a Rule 90(E) warning as he has been treated as a suspect in his prior interviews with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't manage to find the right page that pertains to whether the previous witness was a president -- was the president or just a member of the National Defence Council, so I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: DRAGAN VIDOVIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good evening, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable. Mr. Vidovic, before you start giving evidence, I would like to draw your attention to a particular Rule here at the Tribunal. Under this Rule, Rule 90(E), you may object to answering a question from the Prosecution or the accused or from the Judges if you believe that -- that your answer will incriminate you. When I say "incriminate," I mean that something you say may amount to an admission of your guilt for a criminal offence or could provide evidence that you have committed an offence. However, even if you think your answer will incriminate you and you do not wish to answer the question, the Tribunal has the discretion to oblige you to answer the question, but in such a case, the Tribunal will make it sure that your testimony compelled in such a way shall not be used as evidence in another case against you for any offence other than false testimony. Do you understand, sir, what I have just told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up to a degree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you have any questions, I'll be happy to answer them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: May I please call up 65 ter 90249.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And, sir -- Mr. Vidovic, sir, would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Dragan Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, do you recall meeting with Mr. Nicholls and Mr. Blaszczyk on the 29th of May, 2011, in Belgrade and in the presence of your lawyer Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Did you listen to the audio recording of that 29 May 2011 interview here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And the answers you gave in that 29 May interview, were they accurate and would you provide the same information today?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that the audio recording of the interview along with the English transcript which is uploaded as 65 ter 90249 be admitted as the next exhibit, but I'd ask that it be admitted under seal, and for that I would need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3191 under seal and Exhibit P3192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'll provide a summary of Mr. Vidovic's statement. Mr. Vidovic was assigned to the Karakaj company in Zvornik. The platoon commander was Dragan Ristanovic and the company commander was Milan Blagojevic. The witness was assigned by Commander Ristanovic to guard Karakaj Technical School when he arrived at the school he found paramilitary formations were present including Pivarski. The witness worked three-day shifts. During this time the witness was responsible for guarding approximately 500 to 600 Muslim prisoners held in the big hall of the Karakaj Technical School. The detainees were tightly packed into the hall. Pivarski ordered the witness and other guards to beat the detainees. The witness did not see anyone murdered during his shift or any dead bodies at the school. On the third day, five or six buses from the Drinatrans company arrived. The witness, on order of Commander Ristanovic, travelled on one of the buses to Pilica, the buses were driven under police escort, and the detainees were taken to Pilica Dom Kulture where a lot of soldiers wearing the SMB coloured uniforms were waiting for them. The prisoners went into the Dom and the witness returned to his home in Karakaj. That completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, do you recall testifying in the Grujic trial in Belgrade in 2009?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to ask you a few questions that relate to two topics you discussed in your Grujic testimony. The first topic: Do you recall whether you heard any reports of gunfire from around the school during the time that you were guarding the Karakaj Technical School?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: If I could please have 65 ter number 23241 on the screen and page 24 in the English, page 19 in B/C/S. And where I'm referring is in the middle of the page in B/C/S. And here, Mr. Vidovic, it records questions where the Presiding Judge was asking you about whether you heard something like that was happening and your response, and this is at the top of the English is: "Whether that happened or not -- they say it didn't. Some say there was shooting. I don't know." And then it carries on and the Presiding Judge says: "Who did you hear it from, from the guards or ...?" And your answer was "That was the talk in the village, when there was gunfire around the school." Mr. Vidovic, does that refresh your memory as to whether there was talk around the school that there was gunfire around the school?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I've already said that there was no gunfire when I was there. Now, whether there was any afterwards, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: My question was whether you heard reports of gunfire around the school, not you personally, but whether there was talk of people hearing gunfire around the school.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: You can see the transcript in front of you. Is what you told the Presiding Judge in the Grujic trial accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Where is that? I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: It's in the middle of the page on B/C/S, and it's where the Presiding Judge asks you: "Who did you hear it from, from the guards or ...?" And your answer's recorded as: "That was the talk in the village, when there was the gunfire around the school."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I kindly ask that this be read out verbatim? "They say that there wasn't any, and some people say shooting." I don't know. So over there it says that there was talk and that there wasn't. So why would we skip one of the two variants?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: She read that part earlier on, but I'm not sure whether the witness read that part as well. Now do you see the part, Mr. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you find the question of the Presiding Judge where he asked or she asked: "And when you're not there, did you hear about something like that happening?" And you answered: "Whether that happened or not -- they say it didn't. Some say there was shooting. I don't know." Did you find that part? Why don't we collapse the English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's the first sentence from the top, if I may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And could you read it carefully and then answer the question by Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. I do apologise. My mistake. One further down. One line down. Can the page go down so that we see another answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you read that part, could you let us know so that Ms. Elliott can put you a question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did it happen? Did it not happen? Some people say shooting. Shooting. I don't know. I don't know what to say. While I was there, there was no shooting, and now what people were saying in the village ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the question -- why don't you put your question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Vidovic, is whether you heard any talk around the village of gunfire being heard from the school.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No. Maybe there was talk like that, but no one told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, do you recall tell the Court in Belgrade that you saw a Tamic truck at the Karakaj Technical School?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: First they asked me whether I had seen corpses and whether the truck was taking corpses away, and I said no. And a Tamic was there. I saw it by the school out there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, just to clarify for the record, when you saw that -- when you said that you saw a Tamic was there, that was during your guard duty at the Karakaj Technical School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: But not on at that day. I saw it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And when you say "afterwards," you mean either on the second or third shift that you worked at the Karakaj Technical School?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: This is the last topic I'm going to ask you about, Mr. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I please call up 65 ter 19140A.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, do you recognise what is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Could you please describe for the Court what this photograph shows and how you're familiar with the contents of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the slaughterhouse, Gero's former slaughterhouse. Now it is mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Since when have you owned this facility?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but 2000 -- I'm not sure. Say 2002, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Did you purchase this directly from Mr. Gero, if there is such a person?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. My father, brother, and Gero were there, because the land on which the slaughterhouse was built was owned by my late father. The slaughterhouse was built as a temporary building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are all my questions. I just need to deal with the associated exhibits, and the only one of the associated exhibits I'm tendering is 65 ter 08235 through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we admit the picture first, the photo first?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we come to associated exhibits. There are five of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Two have already been admitted, 23119 was admitted as P3185, and 07232 was admitted as P3186. In terms of the remaining three, I'd like them all admitted but with the rule that it form an integral part of the statement. The only one that I think this witness had any meaningful comment on was 08235, the payroll for the Karakaj company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. So you're tendering only that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3194, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, a small matter. Could we clarify the private session material to open session in light of the answer that was received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you -- could you expand? I don't follow, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, maybe I'm wrong, but I suspected that out of an abundance of caution the Prosecution had asked to go into closed session expecting the witness to give an answer that might reveal the identity of a protected witness, and then the answer didn't reveal the identity of the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I think out of an abundance of caution I would need to go into private session again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Mr. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I should like to thank you for having met with the Defence, and I believe that like in other cases, it will help me be more efficient in the use of time and ask brief questions to get brief answers. Let me start with what you said on page 83. "My father, brother, and Gero were ..." Do you mean to say that they used to be co-owners of that butcher's shop even earlier?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The land belonged to my father, and the provisional building was Gero's property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the late Dragan Ristanovic as a CO, commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that he got killed in combat? You confirmed that in 65 ter 23241, page 4, which is a transcript.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed at Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the transcript, page 58, 65 ter 23241, page 9, did you say that Pivarski put the fear of God into everyone and in his own unit and in the whole town of Zvornik everyone feared him and no one was able to command him?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Precisely. He was all-powerful, as our people say, God himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One page further in the same document did you say that in the Technical School Centre you found people guarding Muslims, wearing camouflage uniforms, carrying automatic weapons, and that was when you heard the names of Pivarski, Mrki, and others?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 13 of the same document, you said that on Pivarski's orders, while Pivarski cursed you and threatened you that he would beat you up, you had to hit three or four prisoners.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. He spoke to me a couple of times with many profanities, and he said he would beat me up if I don't hit them, so I hit three or four people with a police baton just to stay safe myself, to keep out of trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Pivarski's threats were to be taken seriously? He often slapped about his own soldiers. He sometimes stripped them naked. And is it true that he once stripped naked a member of our own civilian authorities, tied him to a goal post at a stadium and beat him?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you want to tell his name, we'll have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That man was tied to a goal post, stripped naked, and beaten up in Celopek. He was beaten by Pivarski and his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it an official of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 18 of the same document, or number 67 of the transcript, you told the commander: "Let us find a way out of here," because nobody dared address Pivarski, and you were trying to make yourself scarce together with the commander. Was it the commander Ristanovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Ristanovic able or did he dare to say anything to Pivarski? Did Ristanovic command Pivarski or the other way around?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Pivarski commanded everyone in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned today and also on that transcript, page 19, that you did not see any of the prisoners suffocate. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you corrected this transcript on page 22, the statement that you had never seen Brano Grujic? Is it true that you never saw Brano Grujic around the Technical School centre?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I don't know how that mistake occurred. Maybe it was interpretation or something. I only heard that Brano Grujic had said to Ristanovic that he would be going for an exchange. It's not that I heard Brano Grujic himself. I heard that Brano Grujic said that to Dragan, and Dragan told me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that on five to six buses, each holding 50 to 60 people, these people were taken from the Technical School to Pilica for their exchange?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was two of those double buses, and in total there were five to six buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, who ordered Mr. Ristanovic to carry out that mission?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Pivarski.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in that period, at that time, there was complete lawlessness in Zvornik, people feared for their lives, Serbs and Muslims equally, and that the authorities in town did not function at all?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Quite right, until they were arrested. There was no law. You had to obey Pivarski and the others who ruled at that time. Until the day when they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say here that both Serbs and Muslims feared for their lives. Were some of the prisoners local Muslims or were they all brought from the mountains?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: There were no local Muslims from Karakaj and Zvornik, only because our neighbours were left alone, lists were made, and they left peacefully going to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Muslims went mostly to Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims, your neighbours, who did not leave for a long time, who were left alone after interviews were conducted with them and remained there to live?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: There was with us a man called Nijaz, originally from Memici, but he had lived for 10, 15 years, perhaps, in Karakaj. He was with us in our company, and he had had interviews at the command and continued there, stayed there for another three or four months, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he then stay as long as he wanted and nobody made any trouble for him?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When were those prisoners taken for that exchange? When they were taken for the exchange, do you know that throughout the war it often happened that the Muslim side rejected an exchange that had been agreed earlier and everything fell through?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Such information was not available to me. I couldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there was one of Pivarski's soldiers on each bus and one local member of the Territorial Defence guarding 50 to 60 people on the bus?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it was in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Pivarski insisted on involving you local people in the beatings and that he wanted to control you because he put one of his own men together with one member of the Territorial Defence on each bus?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, did you feel controlled by Pivarski, you personally, and your men? Did you feel that Pivarski and his group were controlling you?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: All the time. We were constantly supervised by him, and he commanded us, sometimes directly, sometimes through Dragan Avdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that time was there any power in Zvornik able to confront him?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was his activity mostly aimed at Karakaj and the suburbs as opposed to Zuca, who operated in your area? Do you know who Zuca was?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of Zuca. He was the same as the other one. I believe - how do you say it? - with experience. They were experienced. They knew how to go about it, and they scared all of us, and they did as they pleased.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke to the Prosecution also in 2002 and again on the 29th of May, 2011. That's 65 ter 90249.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask if the Prosecution tendered that transcript as well, or is it part of a larger document, larger exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think that has been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the transcript we tendered as his -- this witness's 92 ter statement, 90249 and A would be the public redacted version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was mistaken with the Grujic trial number. Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought we had only Grujic's transcript, so I overlooked this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So on pages 7 and 8 of that document, you said and I will read in English so that you get better interpretation than mine. "[In English] There were paramilitaries on each shift, roughly 10, 15, at any -- any one time. I believed that Grujic, Dragan Spasojevic and Pivarski were responsible for bringing the Muslims -- Muslim prisoners in Karakaj Technical School. The civilian and military police were involved in bringing them to KTS. I heard this from the people I was working with. I cannot remember their names." [Interpretation] And then you say about the Karakaj school, you say yes, and then the question goes – (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can continue now. With the proper redaction.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you had not seen this Brano, whereas the other one took his colleague somewhere? Also, did you hear that this colleague was supposed to mediate in the exchange and that he was sent to Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Brano Grujic, I did not see him. The other one I did see when he

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that's the only time when you saw this man; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The one who got his colleague.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Memici a Muslim village in an area where these people were taken prisoner, those who were detained, that is?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Memici is on the other side, on the road between Zvornik and Tuzla. Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, continue, Mr. Vidovic. Then we come back to you. Yes, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need -- I need to address the issue of redactions. I'm not sure if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's been taken care of. Are we talking about line 17?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes, line 17 and 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When this transport took place, towards Pilica, that is, it was stated that that was for the purposes of an exchange. Did you see any kind of misdeed, any kind of beating or killing in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No. No. I was there only a bit, only while the prisoners got off, and we went back. The bus driver and I went back to Karakaj. Afterwards, I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How is it possible that 50 or 60 detainees are being escorted by only one man, one in front and one in the back, and in what mental state were these detainees?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, when they found out that they were being exchanged, of course they would not make any problems. Everything was all right. There was no excessive behaviour. It was not that they were exhausted or very tired or anything like that. Maybe they looked the way they did because they were told that they were being exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They were a bit more cheerful?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Pivarski could issue orders to the police and give them assignments?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I've already said that he could issue orders to everyone in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that he ordered that two police vehicles escort that convoy to Pilica, and did every bus have two, or did the entire convoy have one vehicle in front and one in the back?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Two vehicles in total, one in front and one in back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked in this same interview, on page 20, whether you knew who the commander of the Territorial Defence of Zvornik was, and you said that you did not know; right?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you also said that you had heard of Marko Pavlovic, but you did not know what position he held.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You only heard the name; right?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that volunteers had the right to a salary and that they were paid by the municipality where they had reported?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they had that right, but they took whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean they prevailed and they took what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: But of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone dare deny them a salary?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Maybe that person who would oppose them would be denied of his life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that most of the territorials and volunteers went into the hills on guard duty, whereas Pivarski and his men were in town?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you go out to guard duty, and how long were your shifts?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I did go on guard duty in seven-day shifts.
